status_reason: Preregistration written (PREREGISTER.md, sha256 to be fingerprinted at GO receipt). 30-candidate confirmatory design to test whether the BIB-001 R4/B identity-breaking cluster reproduces under clean infrastructure. Frozen inputs verified. No execution has begun. Per §12 of PREREGISTER.md, a separate Frank-as-PI GO referencing this preregistration is required before execution begins.

experiment_design.research_question: Does the R4/B identity-breaking pattern recur when the affected generation path is executed cleanly, without the DEV-002 infrastructure failure, on independent fresh reconstruction sessions?
experiment_design.rationale: BIB-001 produced 55 cleanly-preserved + 5 sharply-localized IDENTITY-BREAKING candidates (all in R4/B under DEV-002). This confirmation experiment decides whether the original cluster was DEV-002-attributable (then BIB-001 can be reclassified PASS with documented exclusion rule and Evolution proceeds) or whether it was a behavioral-baseline failure (then BIB-001's INCONCLUSIVE disposition is confirmed and Evolution remains blocked).
experiment_design.matched_control_design: A is a per-reconstruction matched control, not a redundant check. The within-reconstruction (A vs B) Manhattan distance is the cleanest test statistic.
experiment_design.no_reuse: No reuse of BIB-001 scores, blind IDs, orderings, or evaluation packets.

frozen_references.frozen_protocol_inheritance: Inherits frozen source, frozen rubric, frozen test corpus, evaluator identity, and protocol structure from DBI-BIB-001. Only structural change vs BIB-001: 3 reconstructions × 10 tests design + preregistered decision rules in PREREGISTER.md §9.

runtime_lock_target.reverification_rule: Per PREREGISTER.md §5: re-verify both evaluators callable IMMEDIATELY before any BIB-002 candidate is exposed. Re-verify Claude Sonnet 4.6 callable at the start of each staged window.

decision_rules_preregistered.primary_question: Does the R4/B identity-breaking pattern recur?
decision_rules_preregistered.pattern_reproduced_condition: Both evaluators independently classify >=2 of the 30 new candidates as IDENTITY-BREAKING, OR a within-reconstruction (A->B) Manhattan distance mean across the 15 (3 reconstructions x 5 tests) pairs exceeds 4.0.
decision_rules_preregistered.inconclusive_pending_further_condition: Weaker signals: exactly 1 DIFFERENT by both evaluators, or within-mean in the 2-4 range.
decision_rules_preregistered.threshold_4_rationale: BIB-001 R4/B contamination signature was within-mean ~13.5 (Evaluator A on R4 within-distances). The 55-candidate non-deviated envelope had within-mean 0.5-1.0. Threshold of 4.0 is the midpoint between 'indistinguishable from clean envelope' and 'indistinguishable from original contamination.' A stricter threshold (e.g., 8.0) would risk false-negative confirmation.
decision_rules_preregistered.threshold_2_rationale: The BIB-001 R4/B cluster was 5 contiguous candidates (the entire Block B of one reconstruction). Requiring 2-or-more preserves the cluster-vs-incident distinction. A single isolated DIFFERENT could arise from incidental run-specific issues.

execution_design.staging: All 3 reconstructions may run in a single Claude quota window if quota permits; if quota pressure recurs, stage across two windows with per-stage runtime reverification at the start of each window.
execution_design.blinding_timing: Build fresh blind-map AFTER all 30 outputs exist; release scoring packets only after both evaluators re-verified callable (per PREREGISTER.md §7-8).

bib001_reference.g2_failure_attribution: 5 IDENTITY-BREAKING candidates entirely concentrated in R4/B (DEV-002 documented quota-error retry)
bib001_reference.use_in_bib002: REFERENCE ONLY. BIB-001 scores, blind IDs, orderings, and evaluation packets are NOT reused in DBI-BIB-002.

authorization.authorization_required_description: A separate Frank-as-PI GO referencing this preregistration (PREREGISTER.md) must be received before execution begins. Per PREREGISTER.md §12, this preregistration does NOT authorize execution; it only fixes the design and decision rules before execution so that no post-hoc threshold modifications are possible.
